claims.text: A conventionally processed FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse near-surface microstructure.
Controlled cold-spray processing can induce dynamic amorphization in the near-surface region of a FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Cold-spray-induced dynamic amorphization will refine the coating's near-surface microstructure before sliding.
A pre-refined FeNiCrCoCu surface will form an ultra-nanocrystalline adaptive tribolayer during high-temperature sliding.
Formation of a hard tribofilm or tribolayer can contribute to improved wear resistance in a high-entropy-alloy coating.
Microstructural refinement can increase coating hardness through fine-grain strengthening.
Higher coating hardness is associated with reduced wear loss.
Dynamic reconstruction of the pre-refined surface will improve grain-boundary stability.
Improved grain-boundary stability and local hardness will suppress abrupt serrated deformation events during sliding.
High-entropy alloys can exhibit sudden slips visible as stress-drop serrations within certain temperature and strain-rate regimes.
Reducing stress-drop serrations would produce a smoother and more controllable deformation response.
The engineered tribolayer will delay plastic deformation of the conventional-metal substrate.
The engineered coating will have a significantly lower high-temperature sliding wear rate than the conventionally processed coating.
The engineered coating will exhibit fewer or smaller stress-drop serrations than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The proposed wear and deformation effects are expected to hold specifically during high-temperature sliding in an inert or minimally oxidizing environment.
Low-temperature or oxidizing conditions may alter the proposed tribolayer-mediated mechanism.
Variability in substrate-coating adhesion may introduce scatter into wear measurements.
